public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 66

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/66](https://www.erdosproblems.com/66)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace Erdos66

open Filter AdditiveCombinatorics
open scoped Topology

/--
Is there and $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1_A\ast 1_A(n)}{\log n}$$
exists and is $\ne 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_66 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), c ≠ 0 ∧
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ (sumRep A n : ℝ) / Real.log n) atTop (𝓝 c) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the theorems/conjectures for the comments on the page

end Erdos66

review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos66.erdos_66, faithfully asks whether an indicator self-convolution divided by log n converges to a finite nonzero real number. sumRep counts exactly the ordered representations specified by the source. The answer placeholder has the correct scope and polarity, and the source still records the problem as open. Scratch checks compiled without errors or warnings: small representation counts agree with convolution; finite sets cannot supply a nonzero limit; any such limit is nonnegative and therefore positive when nonzero; and the totalized values at n = 0 and n = 1 cannot affect convergence atTop. The source's additional variants are not declarations in this file.
